acceptance_evidence.evidence: The writer fixes ZIP_STORED method, timestamps, flags, extras, comments and the 17-entry order. The parser checks local and central signatures, method, flags, sizes, CRC32, names, offsets, counts and end record, then requires byte equality with a canonical rebuild. Independent review confirmed explicit probes for changed local CRC/path, central CRC/path and central-directory order, along with byte, metadata and current-archive tamper rejection.

acceptance_evidence.area: manifest, component hashes, lineage and replay
acceptance_evidence.evidence: The manifest binds every non-manifest entry's name, media type, byte length and SHA-256. Its manifest digest, ordered lineage leaves and lineage-root digest are cross-checked. Replay canonicalizes JSON entries, reconstructs the input graph, verifies fixed source bytes and authorities, rebuilds the archive byte-for-byte, and reproduces the exact M58 counts and arithmetic.

The SQL writer independently recomputes SHA-256 over archive_bytes and verifies length before insertion. Reads check profile, count and length and run the full archive verifier before returning bytes or metadata. A privileged byte-corruption probe causes a bounded 503 rather than serving corrupted content. Both pack and audit tables force RLS, have composite tenant foreign keys and immutable update/delete triggers, expose member-select only, and revoke writer execution from public and authenticated roles.

acceptance_evidence.area: authorization, tenant isolation and prerequisite gate
acceptance_evidence.evidence: Creation requires an authenticated owner/administrator at both API and SQL layers and an exact approved M58 inventory snapshot whose submitter and reviewer differ. Members can read, download and replay but cannot create. Outsider reads converge on 404 and signed-out access on 401. Direct authenticated writes fail.

Unique tenant/inventory/profile and tenant/idempotency constraints converge duplicate commands. Operation fingerprints bind the immutable request lineage; mismatched reuse and non-equivalent logical duplicates conflict. Tampered replay returns bounded 409, absent data returns 404, and stored-integrity failure returns bounded 503 without private details.

Mutations require allowed origin, bearer identity, exact bodies and bounded file size. Success schemas bind exact profile, entry count, hashes, IDs, totals, completeness and release state. The browser decoders require exact keys and values independent of JSON property order. Download verification computes SHA-256 over received bytes in addition to checking length and response hash header; a same-length changed-byte probe is rejected. UI controls are role/busy gated and status/error output uses live-region semantics.

Server startup requires all M54-M59 flags plus development/test NODE_ENV, and the web component is lazy-loaded only behind all six feature flags. The ordinary production build contains no scanned M59 route/profile/flag/hash/total markers. The UI labels the pack local and synthetic and retains incomplete, release false, fictional bill, unreleased factor/method, no filing, no assurance, no production database and no deployment/release claims.

findings.finding: The initial database read path could return persisted archive bytes and claimed digests without revalidating the archive.
findings.resolution_evidence: Current reads validate profile/count/length and execute the complete archive verifier against stored archive, manifest and lineage digests plus company and inventory lineage before any read/download succeeds; privileged corruption is covered by a bounded-503 lifecycle test.

findings.finding: The initial SQL writer did not independently prove that archive_sha256 described archive_bytes.
findings.resolution_evidence: Migration 0006 now computes encode(sha256(request_archive_bytes),'hex') and rejects any mismatch before persistence.

findings.finding: The initial browser download boundary trusted size and a server-provided digest header, while receipt comparison depended on JSON key insertion order.
findings.resolution_evidence: The browser now computes SHA-256 over downloaded bytes and compares it with hash-bound metadata and the response header. Receipt values are checked by exact keys/values without order dependence; reversed-order acceptance and same-length changed-byte rejection pass.

findings.finding: The initial parser evidence did not explicitly isolate local/central CRC, local/central path and central-entry-order mutations.
findings.resolution_evidence: The focused core suite now mutates each of those fields independently and the strict parser rejects every mutation.

limitations: Persistence and RLS execution evidence uses PGlite, not a hosted Supabase/PostgreSQL deployment; hosted extension availability, grants and operational behavior require later deployment-stage review.
All source data, identities and company records are fixed and synthetic. No customer data or external provider was used.

The reviewer relied on the CEO coordinator's recorded live browser journey and independently inspected accessibility code/tests, but did not repeat a manual assistive-technology, keyboard-only, 200-percent zoom or 390-pixel browser session in this final repair turn.
The ZIP profile is deliberately narrow and internally parsed; interoperability with arbitrary third-party ZIP tooling was not a release criterion and was not exhaustively tested.

The evidence pack preserves an incomplete, unreleased synthetic inventory. It is not assurance evidence, a filing package or proof that factors, methods, Scope 1, Scope 3 or market-based Scope 2 are complete or approved.
